rows: Let us begin with the first step, as one begins with a familiar hymn. Everybody here knows how it goes, so listen for the change.
Brawling is a sin only when it is done for the wrong reason. Tell me your reason.
Risk, to me, is a parable with a hard ending. Learn from it before you live it.
Taking it slow is patience, and patience is a virtue the impatient always forget.
The people came to be told the truth about this match. I will tell it to them.
I judge fairly, and I have judged this contest already.
I have walked to this ring with my conscience clear. Can you say the same?
Behold the stance. It is the stance of a man who has nothing to hide.
You speak of technique. Show me a hold that serves a purpose beyond your own pride.
Strikes are a judgement passed with the fist. Pass them only when they are deserved.
A gamble taken for vanity is a sin of its own. Examine yours before the bell.
A stall is a lie told with the body. I will not tell that lie.
The people deserve a reckoning, not a show. Give them a match they can respect.
You question my moral authority. Let the crowd be the judge of that, and let them judge what they see.
I note the pride you take in your {strength}. Pride goes before a fall. Remember that as we begin.
I have weighed your {strength} carefully, and I find it lighter than you claim.
Steady, as a faithful servant. Then, let it be. A calm man has room to hear the truth.
Agreed, for now, as the parable asks. You have spoken truly, and I acknowledge it.
I could condemn you for that. I would rather invite you to think again.
One fall, as judgement. Keep me down, and I will say the judgement was fair.
On the mat we will be measured, as the old parables teach. Stay with me.
Grounded or standing, the judgement is the same. Do right by the people.
Stay in front of me, and let your conduct speak for you.
A fine answer, measured. It is a true thing, honestly said.
You have not replied, and judgement waits. The truth is waiting for your reply.
Agreed, for now, as the parable asks. I concede a fault of my own there, and I will keep it in mind.
A fair point, and I accept my fault. We will settle it at the bell, where all things are settled.
I will wrestle this match with a clear conscience, and I will leave the judgement to the people.
My approach is plain and honest. You will see the judgement on the night.
Whatever happens, I want the people to leave knowing what they saw was true.
The reckoning is not finished yet. The reckoning is still to come.
I have one more lesson to teach, and you will hear it when the bell rings.
I ought not bear false witness. I cannot give you particulars that establish the charge.
A suspicion is not a judgement. I have no evidence to put before you, and I will not condemn you on that alone.
Then let the accusation rest. Neither of us needs a false judgement before the bell.
A fair distinction. We shall be judged by what we do in the contest, not by an unsupported word.
Let the contest bear witness to our deeds, not to an allegation neither of us can establish.
Pride is easily proclaimed. Watch how each of us conducts ourselves when the advantage passes to the other.
An accusation is not a judgement. What truth about our wrestling can the people witness for themselves?
Let us leave the unproven charge where it belongs. What can our contest bear witness to?
You have heard the words about my {strength}. The lesson will come when you put your answer into practice.
Do not mistake knowledge of my {strength} for victory over them. That would be a rather premature judgement.
A fair correction. We must not pass judgement before the witnesses have spoken.
I concede the point. Let our deeds bear witness, and leave the unsupported charge behind.
